lines.trans: So, look here, Samsonov.
There are five stages of accepting the inevitable.
Denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance.
I didn't understand anything.
Your wife thinks nobody needs you.
That is exactly what she thinks!
We will plant doubts in her.
Then we will provoke jealousy.
We will send her a court summons!
As if you are filing for divorce.
I do not want a real divorce!
The summons will be fake, from a printer.
I don't know, I really doubt it.
I congratulate you, Samsonov, you are henpecked!

meanings.note: Usually как будто. Core Russian conj meaning 'as if, as though' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Он смотрит, как будто знает всё.
examples.trans: He looks as if he knows everything.

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to summon', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.text: Ты же не помнишь ничего. Ты вызвал трезвого водителя!
examples.trans: You don't remember anything, after all. You called a sober driver!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'anger, wrath' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это я тебя специально доводил до гнева.
examples.trans: I was intentionally driving you to anger.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'depression' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'm with my wife this evening.

examples.text: Но вечером я обещал быть с женой.
examples.trans: But I promised to be with my wife this evening.

зародить.gloss: to engender, plant, give birth to

meanings.en: to engender, plant (a doubt or idea)
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'родить'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to engender, plant, give birth to'.

examples.trans: We will plant doubts in her.

examples.text: Эти слова зародили надежду в его сердце.
examples.trans: These words sparked hope in his heart.

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
А именно = namely. Core Russian part meaning 'exactly, namely, precisely' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: Introductory particle/conjunction. Core Russian conj meaning 'so, thus, well then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Итак, у нас конкурс детских поделок.
examples.trans: And so, we have a children's craft contest.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Slang. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fake, counterfeit; linden').
Botanical. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fake, counterfeit; linden').

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'избежный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('inevitable, unavoidable').

examples.trans: There are five stages of accepting the inevitable.

meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
Её, ей, ей, о ней. Core Russian pron meaning 'she; it' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.en: to send (a person, a letter, a message)
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'править'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to send', paired with 'отправлять'.

examples.text: И бабушку на лечение в Израиль отправил.
examples.trans: And he sent our grandmother to Israel for treatment.

meanings.note: Первая стадия — отрицание. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'рицание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'denial, negation' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is the first stage: denial.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Повестка в суд. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'вестка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'summons, subpoena, notice' in everyday Russian.
Повестка дня. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'вестка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'summons, subpoena, notice' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы отправим ей повестку в суд!
examples.trans: We will send her a court summons!

meanings.note: Подавать на развод. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'авать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to serve, submit, file'.
Food or items. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'авать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to serve, submit, file'.

examples.text: Как будто ты подаёшь на развод.
examples.trans: As if you are filing for divorce.

examples.text: Подавай мясо на горячей тарелке гостям.
examples.trans: Serve the meat to the guests on a hot plate.

examples.text: Вика, скорее подавай гостям горячие блюда!
examples.trans: Vika, serve the hot dishes to the guests quickly!

meanings.note: Informal derogatory. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'каблучник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'henpecked husband, pushover' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You are a real henpecked husband!
I congratulate you, Samsonov, you are henpecked!

meanings.note: Поздравляю! = congratulations!. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здравлять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to congratulate', paired with 'поздравить'.

Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нтер'). Common masculine noun meaning 'printer' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I will print the document on a printer.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нятие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'acceptance, adoption' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: пять рублей. Core Russian num meaning 'five' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'jealousy' in everyday Russian.

related.gloss: to be jealous for a while

meanings.note: Stage of grief. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мирение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'humility, resignation, acceptance' in everyday Russian.

Смотреть на + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

TV, a film. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Сомневаться в + prepositional. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'омневаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to doubt', paired with 'усомниться'.

Появились сомнения = doubts arose. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'омнение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'doubt' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У многих из вас появились сомнения.
examples.trans: Many of you have begun to have doubts.
There is no doubt about that.

examples.text: У многих из вас появились сомнения. Хочу сказать вам.
examples.trans: Many of you have begun to have doubts. I want to tell you.

meanings.note: Стадия отрицания = stage of denial. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тадия'). Common feminine noun meaning 'stage, phase' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is the first stage: denial.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'уществовать'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to exist'.

examples.trans: There are five stages of accepting the inevitable.

examples.text: Мы очень часто существуем в иллюзиях.
examples.trans: We very often exist in illusions.

считать.gloss: to count; to think, to consider

meanings.note: посчитать / сосчитать are the perfectives

Я считаю, что... = I think that. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'читать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to count; to think, to consider', paired with 'посчитать'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.

Common masculine noun meaning 'bargaining, trade, haggling' in everyday Russian.
